zero_omission_notes.summary: Explores tangents to a circle, proving radius is perpendicular to tangent at point of contact (Theorem 10.1), and lengths of tangents drawn from an external point are equal (Theorem 10.2).

detailed_sections.full_explanation: Theorem 10.1: The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Radius-Tangent Perpendicularity
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: OP ⊥ XY at point of contact P.

detailed_sections.full_explanation: Theorem 10.2: The lengths of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are equal (PQ = PR).

margin_notes_and_sidebars.title: Equal Tangents
margin_notes_and_sidebars.content: Tangents PQ and PR from external point P are equal.

practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.aim_or_objective: Prove lengths of tangents from external point are equal.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.observations_or_results: Tangents PQ and PR are equal.
practical_lab_activity_or_methodology_ma.conclusion_or_principle: Tangents drawn from external point are equal.

diagrams_figures_and_maps.drawing_or_reading_instructions: Draw circle with center O and rays PQ, PR touching circle.

master_glossary_units_and_formulas.definition_or_meaning: Tangents from external point to circle are equal.
master_glossary_units_and_formulas.example_or_application: If PQ = 10 cm, then PR = 10 cm.

textbook_exercises.question: From point Q, length of tangent to circle is 24 cm and distance from center is 25 cm. Find radius.

objective_questions_1_mark.question: If TP and TQ are tangents to circle with center O so that ∠POQ = 110°, then ∠PTQ is:
objective_questions_1_mark.explanation: Quadrilateral OPTQ has right angles at P and Q => ∠PTQ = 180° - 110° = 70°.

short_answer_questions.question: Prove that in two concentric circles, chord of larger circle touching smaller circle is bisected at point of contact.
short_answer_questions.answer: OP ⊥ AB (radius ⊥ tangent). Perpendicular from center to chord bisects chord => AP = PB.

analytical_reasoning_questions.question: Prove that the tangents drawn at the ends of a diameter of a circle are parallel.
analytical_reasoning_questions.answer: Radius ⊥ Tangent => ∠1 = 90° and ∠2 = 90°. Since alternate interior angles are equal (∠1 = ∠2 = 90°), the tangent lines must be parallel.

comprehensive_long_answers.question: Prove that the parallelogram circumscribing a circle is a rhombus.
comprehensive_long_answers.answer: AB + CD = AD + BC (equal tangent sums). In parallelogram, AB = CD and AD = BC => 2AB = 2AD => AB = AD. Parallelogram with adjacent sides equal is a rhombus.

competency_and_case_studies.case_scenario: Triangle ABC circumscribes circle of radius 4 cm; segments BD and DC are 8 cm and 6 cm.

qa.question: Find sides AB and AC.
qa.answer: Using equal tangents and area equality: AB = 15 cm, AC = 13 cm.

common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.common_error_or_misconception: Thinking a secant and tangent are identical.
common_misconceptions_and_pitfalls.correct_fact_or_method: Secant cuts circle at 2 points; tangent touches circle at exactly 1 point.
